entry_fields.id: stable slug; prose and pin comments cite this, never the number
entry_fields.claim: one sentence, stated the way the book would state it
entry_fields.value: number, [low, high] range, or structured object
entry_fields.source: title / venue / year / locator (doi or url); for papers, the PINNED version
entry_fields.retrieved: ISO date the value was last checked against the source; year-month permitted for entries ported from book.md's reference section, whose figures were last verified July 2026
entry_fields.method: how the value was obtained: quoted, derived, fetched-by-script
entry_fields.fetch: script under registry/fetch/ that can refresh this value, or null for pinned papers
entry_fields.notes: caveats that must travel with the number
entry_fields.book: which book's claims need this entry: book-1 (Part V/method evidence), book-2 (transition/tech/costing), legacy-only (candidate for the deletion manifest's consciously-dropped list); absent = book-1

claims.claim: During Jharkhand's biometric-authentication reforms, 1.5–2 million legitimate beneficiaries lost access to benefits at some point.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar, "Identity Verification Standards in Welfare Programs: Experimental Evidence from India", Review of Economics and Statistics 107(2): 372–392 (2025), doi:10.1162/rest_a_01296
claims.notes: Supersedes NBER WP 26744; the WP-era '~2 million' and the spliced 10%/10.6% quotation are corrected in final-research.md (commit 1bcacc7).

claims.claim: In the reconciliation phase, roughly 1.7 million people did not receive PDS benefits in the first month (July 2017).
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (2025), REStat 107(2), body
claims.notes: ~1.2 million under the paper's conservative assumption. The widely quoted '13%' is a percentage-POINT increase in non-receipt in treated blocks, not a share of all beneficiaries.

claims.claim: 88% of cancelled ration cards sampled in the study districts belonged to genuine households.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (2025), REStat 107(2)
claims.method: quoted; authors label the figure 'purely descriptive' (non-causal)
claims.notes: Covers the 1.44 lakh cancellations in the 10 study districts — never to be narrated as the Drèze survey's 11 lakh statewide figure.

claims.claim: 11 lakh (1.1 million) ration cards were cancelled in Jharkhand for not being linked to Aadhaar.
claims.source: Drèze, Khalid, Khera & Somanchi, "Aadhaar and Food Security in Jharkhand", Economic and Political Weekly 52(50): 50–60 (16 December 2017)
claims.notes: Statewide administrative figure; distinct population from the study-district sample behind muralidharan-2025-genuine-cards.

claims.claim: US permanent-supportive-housing (Housing First) programs show a median benefit-to-cost ratio of 1.8:1.
claims.source: Jacob et al., "Permanent Supportive Housing With Housing First: Findings From a Community Guide Systematic Economic Review", American Journal of Preventive Medicine (2022)
claims.method: quoted (median across studies; median benefit $18,247/person/year vs median cost $16,479)
claims.notes: Corrects the 'Chapman et al. 2021 / 1.44' citation that stood in final-research.md until commit 74920cd.

claims.claim: Housing First produced a median 88% greater decrease in homelessness and a median 41% greater housing stability than Treatment First or usual care.
claims.source: CPSTF effectiveness review, 26 studies, search through February 2018 (thecommunityguide.org, Housing First finding page)
claims.notes: 88% figure rests on 5 studies, 41% on 13. Never merge into an '88% vs 47%' comparison — that garble stood until commit 74920cd.

claims.claim: Controlling for log GDP per capita, the democracy–happiness association collapses from r ≈ 0.51 to a partial r ≈ 0.20: what compresses wellbeing differences across countries is mostly material provision.
claims.source: Derived by registry/fetch/vdem_happiness.py from OWID grapher series (CC BY): electoral-democracy-index (V-Dem v2x_polyarchy), happiness-cantril-ladder (WHR), gdp-per-capita-worldbank; latest common years ≥ 2022; snapshot registry/data/vdem-happiness-2026-08-03.csv
claims.notes: Reproduces the EIU-era narrowing almost exactly (0.195 there) on an openly licensed instrument — the robust half of Part V's worked example. Working record: new-book-plans/vdem-rederivation.md.

claims.claim: Mean life evaluation by Regimes of the World category rises +0.02 (closed→electoral autocracy), +0.59 (→electoral democracy), +1.09 (→liberal democracy): the bottom step buys approximately nothing and the gain concentrates at the top.
claims.source: Same derivation as vdem-2026-democracy-happiness-partial (OWID political-regime series for RoW categories)
claims.notes: The EIU-era step pattern (+0.16/+0.73/+1.01) reproduces on RoW's four categories — the anti-gradualist reading is instrument-robust.

claims.claim: The 'democracy is a floor on wellbeing' dispersion claim is instrument-fragile: on V-Dem polyarchy it survives an income control narrowed (b = −0.49, p = 0.032, log GDP n.s.), while on the same sample and control the EIU index loses it — a claim whose verdict tracks the measuring instrument is not citable as support.
claims.source: Same derivation; isolation test against the alternative index recorded qualitatively in new-book-plans/vdem-rederivation.md (its coefficients stay out of this CC0 registry per the 2026-08-02 licensing ruling)
claims.notes: Part V's worked example, third act: not a clean refutation but instrument-dependence — 'we would have loved this claim, and we cannot have it, and here is exactly why.' Crude heteroskedasticity test kept deliberately (mirrors the original); no HC errors.

claims.claim: The prior democracy/happiness analysis behind Part V's worked example, independently re-derived on openly licensed instruments (source reference only).
claims.source: demo-happy.txt (repository root), computed over democracy_vs_happiness_144.csv: WHR 2025 life evaluations (2022–2024 average) merged with EIU Democracy Index 2025, 144 countries matched from EIU's 166 and WHR's 147
claims.notes: PRIOR ANALYSIS, RECORDED FOR PROVENANCE, NOT AS EVIDENCE. Every figure Part V uses comes from the V-Dem re-derivation (vdem-2026-*), and no EIU-derived value enters this CC0 registry, per the 2026-08-02 licensing ruling. The re-derivation reproduced the income narrowing and the step pattern and did NOT reproduce this analysis's headline dispersion finding — see vdem-2026-floor-claim-instrument-fragile. The merged CSV sits in the repository root under the root LICENSE, committed before that ruling, and carries EIU index values; whether the repository may grant CC0 over a non-redistributable index is an open question for the author, recorded in CLAUDE.md under the pending obligations that outlived the retired root tracker.
